name: Bigin by Zoho
tagline: A stripped-down CRM from Zoho aimed at small teams who found Zoho CRM itself too much.

pricing.basis: per user per month, billed annually
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Bigin has a free single-user tier and paid tiers roughly in the 7 to 12 USD per user range, with separate INR pricing on the .in domain.

verdictSummary: The core of Bigin is a contacts table, a deals table, a few pipeline stages you can drag cards between, and activity notes. That is genuinely a one-sitting build and an agent will nail it. What takes it from a weekend to a slog is everything hanging off the edges: two-way email sync, telephony, WhatsApp threads, mobile apps your team will actually open, and the workflow rules that fire when a deal moves stage. If you are one person tracking thirty deals, build it and never think about seats again. If you are five people who need the same record to update when someone sends an email from their phone, you are rebuilding a sync engine, not a CRM.
coreLoopDIY: A local kanban pipeline of deals with linked contacts, stage history, notes and follow-up reminders, backed by SQLite.
requirements: A place to run it: laptop, a small VPS, or a home server
Optional: an IMAP mailbox if you want email logging
Optional: Tailscale or similar if more than one person needs access
whatYouLose: Two-way email sync and the ability to log a thread without copy-pasting it
Mobile apps, which is where most sales notes actually get typed
Telephony and WhatsApp integration, plus call logging
Workflow automation and reminders that fire whether or not your laptop is awake
The rest of the Zoho ecosystem: Books, Desk, Campaigns, and the single sign-on that ties them
moatNotes: Bigin's pull is not the pipeline UI, it is the mail, phone and Zoho Books plumbing plus a mobile app your least technical colleague will tolerate.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a CRM's value shows up on someone else's phone, not on your dev machine. Bigin is cheap enough that a two-person shop pays for it out of pocket-change, and it comes with the email connector, the mobile client, the call logging and the Zoho account you probably already have for invoicing. Rebuilding that plumbing is not hard in a clever way, it is hard in a boring, endless, keep-tokens-fresh way. The DIY version wins exactly when the CRM has one user and that user is you.
notes: A personal pipeline tracker is one of the highest hit-rate agent builds there is; a team CRM is not the same product wearing a different hat.
prompt:
Build a single-tenant personal CRM that runs locally. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with server actions
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/crm.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Tailwind for styling, dnd-kit for drag and drop
- Zero auth. It binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.

Data model:
- contacts: id, name, email, phone, company, title, notes, created_at
- companies: id, name, domain, notes
- pipelines: id, name; stages: id, pipeline_id, name, sort_order
- deals: id, title, contact_id, company_id, pipeline_id, stage_id, amount_cents, currency, expected_close, status (open/won/lost), lost_reason, created_at, updated_at
- activities: id, deal_id, contact_id, kind (note/call/meeting/email), body, occurred_at
- tasks: id, deal_id, title, due_at, done_at
- stage_events: id, deal_id, from_stage_id, to_stage_id, moved_at

Screens:
1. Pipeline board: columns are stages, cards are deals showing title, company, amount, days in stage. Drag to move, which writes a stage_event. Column headers show count and summed amount.
2. Deal detail: editable fields, activity timeline, add note, add task, mark won or lost.
3. Contacts and companies: searchable list plus a detail page showing linked deals and activities.
4. Today: tasks due or overdue, plus deals with no activity in 14 days flagged as stale.
5. Reports: won/lost counts and value by month, average days per stage, conversion rate per stage.

Also build:
- Seed script with one default pipeline (Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed) and a handful of fake deals
- CSV import for contacts and CSV export for deals
- A JSON backup endpoint that dumps the whole database
- Full-text search across contacts, companies, deals and activity bodies using SQLite FTS5

Explicitly out of scope: email sync, calendar sync, telephony, multi-user, permissions, mobile apps, workflow automation. Do not stub them, do not add menu items for them.

Secrets, if any are ever needed, go in .env and .env.example. Ship a README with setup, seed, and backup instructions.
